title: Closed factorization locus for a finite locally free source
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $q:D\to S$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and let $X\to S$ be affine and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a finitely presented closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $S$-scheme $P$ and every $S$-morphism $F:D\times_SP\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], there exists a finitely presented closed immersion $L\hookrightarrow P$ such that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $t:T\to P$, the morphism $t$ factors through $L$ if and only if $F\circ(1_D\times t):D\times_ST\to X$ factors through $Z$. These factorizations are unique. For every morphism $P'\to P$, the locus for the induced family on $D\times_SP'$ is $L\times_PP'$ with its given closed immersion. No smoothness or connectedness hypothesis on $D$, $P$ or $Z$ is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Lemma 2.1.3 and its proof, printed pp.58--59, and proof of Proposition 2.1.2, p.60, closed immersion of Hom functors obtained by coefficient equations for the ideal of the target. Pullback by the specified family gives this parameter-locus formulation. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this exact assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-finite-pushforward-locally-free], cover $S$ by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ on which $q_*\mathcal O_D$ is free of some finite rank $r$, allowed to vary between charts. The finite morphism $q$ is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so $D_U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with a chosen $A$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $B$. Since $X\to S$ is affine, $X_U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Cover the inverse images of these $U$ in $P$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $D\times_SV=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A R)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free], $B_R=B\otimes_A R$ has basis $e_a\otimes1$. The given family restricts to $F_V:D\times_SV\to X_U$, corresponding to an $A$-algebra map $\phi:C\to B_R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. The map is $A$-linear because $F_V$ is over $U$.

source.place: Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat); Tag 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); Conrad Lemma 2.1.3, printed pp.58–59, local finite-free reduction.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I$ be the ideal sheaf of $Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Since this immersion is finitely presented, [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal] says that $\mathcal I$ is of finite type. Its restriction to $X_U$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-finite-type-generating-sections], choose finitely many $h_1,\ldots,h_m\in I=\mathcal I(X_U)$ generating this ideal. The affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies $Z\times_X X_U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$. Put $j_\beta=\phi(h_\beta)\in B_R$ and $J=(j_1,\ldots,j_m)\subseteq B_R$.

Write $j_\beta=\sum_{a=1}^r c_{\beta a}(e_a\otimes1)$, with $c_{\beta a}\in R$, and let $K_V=(c_{\beta a})\subseteq R$. This is the coefficient ideal of all of $J$, not only of the listed generators: for $b\in B_R$, multiplication by $b$ is an $R$-linear matrix, so every coefficient of $bj_\beta$ is an $R$-linear combination of the $c_{\beta a}$. Finite sums give the same assertion for every $j\in J$. Conversely each $c_{\beta a}$ is a coordinate functional evaluated on $j_\beta\in J$. Every $R$-linear functional is a linear combination of the coordinate functionals, so $K_V$ is exactly the ideal generated by all $\lambda(j)$ for $j\in J$ and $\lambda:B_R\to R$ linear. In particular it is generated by the $mr$ displayed elements. Define $L_V=\operatorname{Spec}(R/K_V)\hookrightarrow V$, a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0B97, lemma-hilb-d-of-closed, final paragraph: coefficients of generators in a finite free basis. Here the pulled-back ideal has finitely many generators, so the coefficient ideal does too.

proof.text: For any $R$-algebra $R'$, the algebra $B_R$ is finite free, hence finite projective: it is a direct summand of itself [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Apply [lem-pc-affine-containment-ideal] to $B_R$ and $J$. It says that $J$ maps to zero in $B_R\otimes_RR'$ if and only if $K_V$ maps to zero in $R'$. On the one hand, a map $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to V$ factors through $L_V$ exactly when $R\to R'$ kills $K_V$. On the other hand, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] and the affine tensor description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the map $D\times_S\operatorname{Spec}R'\to X_U$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$ exactly when the composite $C\to B_R\to B_R\otimes_RR'$ kills $I$, equivalently its generators $j_\beta$. Thus the required equivalence holds for affine $V$-tests. No flatness of $R'$ is required. On a base change $R\to R\prime$, the composite on sections is explicitly $c\mapsto\phi(c)\otimes1$, so the same ideal $J$ is being tested.

source.place: Tag 0B97, lemma-hilb-d-of-closed, final paragraph: coefficients of generators in a finite free basis. Here the pulled-back ideal has finitely many generators, so the coefficient ideal does too.

proof.text: The equivalence just proved holds for every scheme $T\to V$, not only affine ones. Cover $T$ by affine opens, apply Step 4 on each, and use [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to identify the resulting open cover of $D\times_ST$. Both closed immersions $L_V\hookrightarrow V$ and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ are monomorphisms by [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed]. Their local factorizations therefore agree on overlaps. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], they glue to unique global factorizations in each direction. This proves the equivalence and uniqueness for all $V$-tests.

source.place: Tags 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace), 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); globalization of the coefficient construction of pic.tex Tag 0B97.

proof.text: For two chosen parameter charts $V,W$, set $O=V\cap W$, without assuming $O$ affine. The restrictions $L_V\times_VO\hookrightarrow O$ and $L_W\times_WO\hookrightarrow O$ are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Step 5 gives them the same universal property on every $O$-scheme. Test it on each of these two schemes: each inclusion factors uniquely through the other. Their two composites are identities since the inclusions are monomorphisms [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed]. Thus there is a unique isomorphism over $O$ between these restrictions. On triple overlaps the two comparison composites agree by the same uniqueness; hence the cocycle condition holds.

source.place: Tags 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace), 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); globalization of the coefficient construction of pic.tex Tag 0B97.

proof.text: Use the inverse images of $V\cap W$ in the $L_V$ as overlap opens and the isomorphisms from Step 6 as transitions. They satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes], so they glue to a scheme $L$. The maps $L_V\to V\to P$ agree on overlaps and glue to $l:L\to P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Its inverse image of $V$ is exactly $L_V$: a point in another chart $L_W$ mapping into $V$ lies in the overlap over $W\cap V$, where it is identified with a point of $L_V$. Since $L_V\to V$ is affine with surjective coordinate map $R\to R/K_V$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] shows that $l$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tags 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace), 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); globalization of the coefficient construction of pic.tex Tag 0B97.

proof.text: The ideal sheaf of $l$ restricts on every chosen $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ to $\widetilde{K_V}$ by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Step 3 exhibits finitely many generators of $K_V$, which generate $\widetilde{K_V}$; hence this ideal sheaf is locally of finite type (also [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]). Apply [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal] to conclude that $L\hookrightarrow P$ is of finite presentation. This is local finite generation on $P$; no finite open cover of $P$ or Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

For any $t:T\to P$, the opens $t^{-1}(V)$ cover $T$. On each one Step 5 gives the equivalence between factorization through $L_V$ and factorization of the restricted $F_T$ through $Z$. The inverse images $D\times_St^{-1}(V)$ cover $D\times_ST$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product]. As in Step 5, the local factorizations agree because $l$ and $i$ are monomorphisms [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed], and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them. This proves exactly the stated universal property on arbitrary $T$, with both factorizations unique.

source.place: Tags 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace), 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes); globalization of the coefficient construction of pic.tex Tag 0B97.

proof.text: Finally let $P'\to P$ be arbitrary. Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ of its inverse image of $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the pulled-back source has basis $e_a\otimes1$ by [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The pulled-back $j_\beta$ has coefficients equal to the images of $c_{\beta a}$ in $R'$. Thus its coefficient ideal is $K_VR'$. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image], the given immersion $L\times_PP'\hookrightarrow P'$ has exactly these local ideals. They are finitely generated, so [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal] again gives finite presentation. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies maps to $L\times_PP'$ over $P'$ with factorizations through $L$ of their composites to $P$. Step 9 identifies these with factorizations of the induced family through $Z$, proving the claimed base-change compatibility, including uniqueness. Empty sources ($r=0$) give $K_V=0$ and $L_V=V$; every calculation remains valid.
